steps.intent: Our objective is to anchor the October ceasefire, secure the release of all living hostages and remains, condemn Hamas, and keep humanitarian and governance tracks under US leadership. We expect Algeria and Pakistan to press for stronger condemnation of Israel and explicit UNRWA language, while China and Russia may abstain rather than veto a US draft that supports the ceasefire. The main challenge is retaining enough balance on humanitarian and two-State language to reach nine votes without compromising core US red lines.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the effort to consolidate the ceasefire and will engage constructively, but the current text remains unbalanced. We cannot accept the self-defence paragraph or one-sided condemnation; the Council must also condemn Israeli violations, settler terrorism and the blockade. We request balanced language on accountability, UNRWA, full withdrawal, and the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines with East Jerusalem as the capital.
messages.China: China supports the draft as a basis, but it must send an unambiguous message for an immediate and permanent ceasefire and the lifting of the blockade, and it must be balanced in condemning all attacks against civilians. We ask the penholder to incorporate explicit support for UNRWA and UN humanitarian coordination, reject militarized aid mechanisms, condemn settler violence and halt settlement activity, and avoid language that prejudges Gaza’s governance or Palestinian self-determination. China is ready to work constructively on these amendments.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the direction of the text and its clear condemnation of Hamas, hostage-taking and the use of civilians. We nevertheless need OP4 to explicitly require the lifting of restrictions on aid and guaranteed access for UNRWA and humanitarian partners, and OP1 to anchor the process in a permanent ceasefire. We also ask for explicit language on settler violence and settlement expansion in the West Bank, and stand ready to work with the United States and E10 colleagues.
messages.France: France supports the US draft as a basis for adoption and thanks the penholder. We ask that OP1 reflect France's consistent call for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire, and that OP4 explicitly uphold humanitarian principles and the work of UN agencies, including UNRWA. France also asks that OP6 state clearly that Hamas must lay down its arms and cannot be part of the solution in Gaza, and that OP8 condemn settler violence and settlement expansion in the West Bank.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the United States for presenting a basis for the Council to act. We support the text with changes to make clear that the ceasefire must lead to a permanent end to hostilities, to ensure UNRWA and UN humanitarian agencies can operate safely and at scale throughout Gaza, including the north, and to strengthen language on settler violence and illegal settlements. We also ask the penholder to include explicit support for the Egypt-Qatar-United States mediation and the resumption of phase-two negotiations.
messages.Guyana: Guyana welcomes the United States draft as a basis for the Council to speak with one voice. We ask that OP1 reflect the repeated demand for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire and that the text expressly reaffirm UNRWA's central humanitarian role. We also seek balanced accountability for all violations by all parties, including Israeli forces and settlers, and stronger two-State language consistent with international law and relevant resolutions. With these changes, Guyana can support the text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the ceasefire and humanitarian thrust of the draft but cannot accept a one-sided text. We require balanced condemnation of all violations, explicit action on the blockade and UNRWA access, and deletion of language that prejudges Gaza's governance or Palestinian self-determination. These changes are necessary for Pakistan's support.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft as a basis and appreciates the penholder's efforts. We ask that OP1 make the ceasefire explicitly immediate and sustained, that OP4 include lifting restrictions on humanitarian access and restoring essential services, and that OP8 add balanced language condemning all violence against civilians, including settler violence, and calling for accountability. These changes would align the text with resolution 2735 (2024) and Panama's consistent calls for humanitarian access and protection of civilians.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea appreciates the United States' efforts to consolidate Council support around the 13 October ceasefire and the release of hostages. We can support the text with concrete improvements to ensure humanitarian access is delivered according to humanitarian principles and through the UN system, and to make the ceasefire and accountability provisions balanced and operational. We would also welcome explicit reference to the recent Israeli airstrikes and settler violence so that the Council speaks clearly to all violations on the ground.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the ceasefire and humanitarian objectives of this draft, but the text remains unbalanced and cannot be supported in its current form. We require explicit condemnation of Israeli violations, including settler violence and attacks on civilians, a clear demand to lift the humanitarian blockade of Gaza, and balanced security and governance language that does not prejudge Palestinian internal arrangements. We are ready to work constructively, but these elements are necessary for our support.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone welcomes the United States draft and supports its adoption, as it reflects the 13 October ceasefire and the priority of humanitarian access. To ensure the text is balanced and implementable, we request that OP1 refer to an immediate, permanent and unconditional ceasefire, that OP4 require access through all crossings without restrictions, and that OP8 explicitly address settler violence and all ceasefire violations. We also ask for a new operative paragraph calling for an independent and impartial investigation into attacks on civilians and humanitarian personnel, including at aid distribution sites.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports this draft as a basis and welcomes its focus on the ceasefire, hostages, humanitarian access and the two-State solution. We ask the penholder to strengthen balanced language on protection of civilians and accountability for all violations, to ensure humanitarian access through all crossings including Rafah and for UNRWA, and to make clear that forced displacement and demographic change are rejected in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. These changes are essential for Slovenia’s support.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft as a basis and welcomes its focus on the 13 October ceasefire and humanitarian access. We ask that OP1 explicitly reaffirm an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire consistent with resolution 2735, and that OP4 require the lifting of all restrictions on aid and reference UNRWA’s indispensable role. We also need balanced language in OP2 and OP8 condemning all violations, including Israeli attacks and settler violence, and demanding an end to settlement expansion.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports this text and welcomes its condemnation of Hamas, its demand for the release of all hostages, and its humanitarian and two-State commitments. We ask for targeted amendments on ICRC access to all remaining hostages, reopening all crossings including Rafah and Kerem Shalom with unimpeded UN and humanitarian operations, explicit condemnation of settler violence, and clear language that Hamas has no role in Gaza's future governance. These changes reflect long-standing UK positions and would strengthen the text; we are ready to work with the United States and all Council members to finalise it.

replies.Guyana: partially accepted: tied two-State language to international law and permanent endpoint to 2735, but rejected UNRWA centrality and explicit Israeli forces/settlers accountability.
replies.Pakistan: partially accepted: added self-defence caveat and West Bank language, but retained strong Hamas condemnation and exclusion from control.
replies.Panama: accepted: incorporated immediate/sustained ceasefire, dignified release, aid restrictions and settler-violence accountability.
replies.Republic of Korea: partially accepted: added humanitarian principles, all-crossings access and West Bank language; did not explicitly name Israeli forces.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: added generic condemnation of all violations, humanitarian-access language and Palestinian governance language, but rejected explicit Israeli-attack and blockade wording.
replies.Sierra Leone: partially accepted: accepted permanent-endpoint, unrestricted-crossings and settler-violence language, but omitted a new independent investigation mechanism.
replies.Slovenia: partially accepted: accepted IHL principles, Rafah/Kerem Shalom access, West Bank forced-displacement and detainee language, but omitted UNRWA and full West Bank territorial-change language.
replies.Somalia: partially accepted: accepted permanent endpoint tied to 2735, all-parties ceasefire condemnation and aid restrictions, but omitted UNRWA and settlement-expansion cessation.
replies.United Kingdom: partially accepted: incorporated ICRC access, all-crossings access, settler violence and Hamas no-governance role, but did not name UNRWA.

steps.summary: The revised text preserves strong condemnation of Hamas, hostage-release demands and Israel's self-defence while adding targeted humanitarian-access, ceasefire-implementation, accountability and West Bank language. It should attract broad support while avoiding a P5 veto; Algeria and Pakistan are expected to oppose, with China, Russia and Guyana abstaining.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the reference to the 13 October ceasefire and the partial acceptance of balanced accountability and displacement language. However, we cannot support a text that reaffirms a self-defence clause used to justify collective punishment, fails to condemn explicitly Israeli attacks on civilians, and omits the 1967 borders and East Jerusalem. We also insist on naming UNRWA and ending the blockade, and on removing language that externally dictates Gaza's governance; these are consistent with resolution 2735 and the Council's previous positions.
messages.China: China supports the draft as a basis for Council action but asks the penholder to strengthen the ceasefire and humanitarian provisions, including by naming UNRWA and rejecting militarized aid mechanisms. Language in OP8 prejudges Palestinian internal governance and should be balanced in favour of reconciliation and PA unity. China also seeks an explicit call to halt settlement activities and ensure accountability for settler violence.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the revised text and thanks the penholder for incorporating the permanent-endpoint language, the lifting of aid restrictions, and settler violence. We still need an explicit reference to UNRWA in OP6: given the legal and operational attacks on the Agency, referring only to “United Nations agencies” is insufficient, and this remains a red line for us. We also ask that OP10 call for an immediate end to settlement expansion, which is central to preserving the two-State solution. With those changes, Denmark can support the text.
messages.France: France welcomes the revised text and the acceptance of Hamas disarmament language, humanitarian principles and settler violence. We cannot, however, accept language that falls short of an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire; OP1 must reflect that clearly. We also ask for explicit protection of UNRWA's role and a clear condemnation of settlement expansion. With these changes France is ready to support the resolution.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the broad thrust of the revised text and welcomes the acceptance of language on mediation, access to all parts of Gaza, and settler violence. To preserve the text’s humanitarian and legal balance, we ask the penholder to include an explicit reference to UNRWA in OP6 and to add clear language that Israeli settlements are illegal under international law and that settlement expansion is condemned. These are consistent with Greece’s longstanding position and with the Council’s relevant resolutions.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the overall objective of the United States text and welcomes the ceasefire agreement, but we cannot support the draft as it stands without a clear immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire and an affirmation of UNRWA's central humanitarian role. We also seek explicit accountability for violations by Israeli forces and settlers, and language on settlement activity and Palestinian self-determination in the two-State paragraph. We remain ready to work constructively with the penholder and all members to strengthen the text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan appreciates the penholder's partial acceptance of the self-defence caveat and West Bank language. However, the text remains unbalanced: it must not single out Hamas while failing to name Israeli airstrikes and settler violence, and it cannot dictate Palestinian internal governance by excluding Hamas or any Palestinian faction. Pakistan requests the changes above and can support the draft if they are reflected.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the revised draft. It reflects our core priorities: an immediate and sustained ceasefire, the immediate, dignified and unconditional release of all hostages, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and accountability for settler violence. We appreciate the penholder's constructive engagement and urge the Council to preserve this balanced text and act without further delay.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea welcomes the penholder's partial incorporation of our earlier proposals, particularly on humanitarian principles, all-crossings access and West Bank language. We continue to believe that humanitarian access should be explicitly channelled through the United Nations humanitarian system and that accountability language should cover documented violations by Israeli forces as well as settlers. With those adjustments, we are prepared to support the text.
messages.Russian Federation: We appreciate the partial incorporation of our proposals, but the draft remains unbalanced. We cannot support it without an explicit condemnation of Israeli attacks against civilians in Gaza and the West Bank and a demand for the immediate lifting of the humanitarian blockade under UN coordination. We also insist on language affirming Palestinian self-determination without external imposition and on convening an international peace conference to end the occupation. If these points are reflected, we will support the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone welcomes the revision and appreciates the penholder's acceptance of language on a permanent endpoint, unrestricted crossings and settler violence. We remain concerned that the text still lacks the independent investigation we previously requested into attacks on civilians and humanitarian personnel, including civilians seeking assistance. We also believe OP1 should expressly describe the ceasefire as unconditional. Sierra Leone is prepared to support the draft with these important improvements.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholder for incorporating the Rafah/Kerem Shalom access, IHL principles, and West Bank/detainee language. We can support the text with two remaining fixes: UNRWA must be explicitly protected and granted unimpeded access, and the rejection of demographic or territorial change must cover the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, not only Gaza. These are red lines for us because they go to the viability of the two-State solution and the protection of Palestinian civilians.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholder for the partial revisions, particularly on the ceasefire endpoint and humanitarian access. We can support the text if OP6 explicitly names UNRWA and protects its mandate and operations; this remains a red line for us given the agency’s indispensable humanitarian role. We also ask that OP10 expressly demand the cessation of settlement activities and settler violence. With those changes, Somalia is ready to vote in favour.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the penholder's revisions, which now reflect our calls on ICRC access, all crossings including Rafah and Kerem Shalom, settler violence, and Hamas's exclusion from Gaza's future governance. We remain concerned that UNRWA is not explicitly named, given its indispensable humanitarian role in Gaza; we ask that OP6 refer to 'United Nations agencies, including UNRWA'. With that addition, the United Kingdom is ready to support the resolution.

replies.China: partially accepted: accepted permanent ceasefire, UNRWA and settlement language, but retained Hamas exclusion and did not reject all aid mechanisms
replies.Denmark: accepted: UNRWA explicitly named and settlement expansion addressed
replies.France: accepted: OP1 permanent ceasefire, UNRWA, and settlement expansion condemnation included
replies.Greece: partially accepted: UNRWA and settlement expansion included, but omitted 'illegal under international law'
replies.Guyana: partially accepted: OP1 permanent ceasefire and accountability for Israeli forces included, but no standalone UNRWA centrality/funding paragraph
replies.Pakistan: partially accepted: added all armed groups and UNRWA, but retained Hamas exclusion and did not single out Israeli airstrikes
replies.Panama: accepted: no changes requested and key priorities retained
replies.Republic of Korea: accepted: UN humanitarian system and violence by Israeli forces included
replies.Russian Federation: rejected: did not single out Israeli attacks, demand lifting blockade, or convene international peace conference
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: unconditional ceasefire and independent investigations included
replies.Slovenia: accepted: UNRWA and West Bank/East Jerusalem demographic-change language included
replies.Somalia: accepted: UNRWA named and settlement cessation language included
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: UNRWA explicitly named in OP6

steps.summary: The revised text accepts key P5 and humanitarian requests while preserving US red lines on Hamas condemnation and exclusion, self-defence, and phased implementation. It is expected to be adopted with 10 votes in favour, 2 against and 3 abstentions, with no negative vote from a permanent member.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria will support a resolution that reinforces the ceasefire and humanitarian relief, while using its explanation of vote to register unmet red lines on self-defence, Israeli strikes, the 1967 borders and East Jerusalem.
reasons.China: China had expressed support with changes, and the penholder accepted key elements such as permanent ceasefire language, UNRWA support, and settlement references. Given the resolution’s positive ceasefire and humanitarian provisions, China would not block it despite remaining reservations over the Hamas exclusion clause.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark’s red-line request explicitly naming UNRWA and its important request on settlement expansion were accepted, and the draft aligns with Denmark’s record supporting ceasefire, hostages, humanitarian access, international law, and the two-State solution.
reasons.France: France’s requested red-line change on an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire was accepted, along with its priorities on UNRWA and settlement expansion, and the draft broadly aligns with France’s established position on humanitarian access, hostage release and the two-State solution.
reasons.Greece: Greece has consistently supported Council action for a ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, UNRWA, and the two-State solution, and its key requests were partially reflected. Voting in favour aligns with Greece’s foreign-policy commitments, with a public interpretive note on settlement illegality.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported Council texts demanding a ceasefire, humanitarian access, and protection of Palestinian civilians; this draft now includes its key red-line language on a permanent ceasefire and accountability, and it expressly references UNRWA and humanitarian funding even without a standalone centrality paragraph. Voting in favour is therefore consistent with Guyana’s established position while allowing it to flag remaining concerns.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan's red-line requests on OP3 and OP8 were not met; the final text still singles out Hamas and omits explicit condemnation of Israeli airstrikes, making support inconsistent with Pakistan's established position.
reasons.Panama: Panama had already signalled support with no changes requested, and the draft retains its key priorities on ceasefire, hostages, humanitarian access, international law and the two-State solution. It therefore votes in favour and explains that support before the vote.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions on this agenda item, and its requested changes on UN humanitarian system access and violence by Israeli forces were accepted. A vote in favour aligns with Seoul’s support for implementation of the 13 October ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian relief, accountability, and the two-State solution.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia’s core red-line amendments on equal condemnation of Israeli attacks and an explicit demand to lift the Gaza blockade were rejected, leaving the US draft unbalanced from Moscow’s perspective. Abstention avoids vetoing a ceasefire implementation text while signalling dissatisfaction with its pro-Israel tilt and external governance prescriptions.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported Council action demanding a ceasefire, humanitarian access and accountability, and its key requested changes on an unconditional ceasefire and independent investigations were incorporated. No pre-vote statement is needed, consistent with its practice of explaining votes after adoption.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia’s red-line requests were accommodated, and the text aligns with its consistent support for ceasefires, humanitarian access including UNRWA, rejection of demographic change, and the two-State solution. Slovenia would therefore vote in favour.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia has consistently supported Gaza ceasefire and humanitarian resolutions, and its key red-line request on UNRWA and important request on settlements were accepted. The draft aligns with its foreign policy priorities on civilian protection, humanitarian access and the two-State solution.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft reflects the UK’s priorities on the ceasefire, hostage release, humanitarian access, UNRWA, accountability and the two-State solution, and the UK’s requested UNRWA language was accepted. The UK would therefore vote in favour and explain its vote before the Council.
reasons.United States of America: The draft is United States-authored and advances core U.S. policy: condemning Hamas, supporting Israel’s right to self-defence while pressing humanitarian access and ceasefire implementation, and reaffirming the two-State solution. With broad Council support in negotiations, the United States would vote yes.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because it demands the immediate, full and expeditious implementation of the 13 October ceasefire, the release of all remaining hostages and return of remains, the withdrawal of Israeli forces as provided for in the agreement, unhindered humanitarian access at scale, and it rejects forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. These are urgent and overriding obligations. However, Algeria’s support cannot be read as acceptance of the imbalances in this text. We regret that the Council again fails to speak clearly on the root causes of this crisis, including the occupation, and that the draft does not explicitly affirm the pre-1967 borders with East Jerusalem as the capital of the State of Palestine, nor condemn the indiscriminate Israeli attacks against civilians in Gaza. Algeria interprets all references to self-defence strictly in accordance with international law. Self-defence can never justify collective punishment, forced displacement, the denial of humanitarian access or violations of international humanitarian law. We call for full respect for the ceasefire by all parties, protection of civilians, accountability for all violations, including settler violence and attacks on holy sites, an immediate end to the blockade of Gaza, and the unimpeded operation of UNRWA and all humanitarian agencies. Algeria will continue to stand with the Palestinian people until they achieve their inalienable right to self-determination and an independent State with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
before.China: China supports the draft resolution and will vote in favour. The adoption of this resolution, though not perfect, would send a clear signal in favour of an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access, and the rejection of forced displacement and settlement expansion. China has consistently called for an immediate ceasefire, the lifting of restrictions on humanitarian supplies, the full support of UNRWA and other United Nations humanitarian agencies, and a two-State solution. We regret that some of our reasonable proposals were not fully incorporated. In particular, the future of Gaza and the question of Palestinian governance must ultimately be decided by the Palestinian people themselves through inclusive intra-Palestinian reconciliation; Security Council action should not prejudge this question or divide the Palestinian people. We also stress that humanitarian assistance must be delivered through the United Nations and humanitarian agencies and must not be militarized or politicized. China will continue to work with Council members to promote a comprehensive, just and lasting settlement of the Palestinian question.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the ceasefire agreement of 13 October and the release of living hostages and Palestinian detainees, and we call for its immediate, full and expeditious implementation. The humanitarian situation in Gaza remains catastrophic: all crossings must be opened, aid must flow at scale and in accordance with humanitarian principles, and the safe and sustained operation of United Nations agencies, including UNRWA, and humanitarian partners must be ensured. We stress the need for the immediate and dignified release of all remaining hostages and the return of the remains of all deceased hostages, for accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, and for an immediate end to settlement expansion. Denmark remains firmly committed to the two-State solution and to unifying Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority.
before.France: Mr. President, France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome that the text demands an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire consistent with resolution 2735 (2024), the release of all remaining hostages and the return of the remains of the deceased, and immediate, safe and unhindered humanitarian access at scale, including through the United Nations system and UNRWA. France unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 committed by Hamas; the hostages must be released immediately and unconditionally. We also welcome the text’s clear rejection of forced displacement and demographic or territorial change, its condemnation of settler violence and settlement expansion, and its renewed commitment to the two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. France calls on all parties to implement the ceasefire agreement fully and without delay, and on the Council to speak with one voice. We urge all members to support this text.
before.Greece: Mr. President, Greece will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the focus on the immediate, full and expeditious implementation of the ceasefire agreement, the unconditional release of all remaining hostages, and the urgent need for safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access at scale, including through UNRWA and humanitarian partners. Greece has consistently condemned the horrific terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023 and continues to call for accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law. We also welcome the references to rejecting forced displacement and demographic or territorial change, to countering settler violence, and to the two-State solution. While Greece would have preferred an explicit reaffirmation that Israeli settlements are illegal under international law, we believe this resolution advances essential humanitarian and political objectives and must be supported. We urge all parties to comply with their obligations and to return fully to negotiations in good faith.
before.Guyana: Mr. President, Guyana thanks the United States for its efforts to bring the Council together on a text that responds to the catastrophic situation in Gaza. We welcome the inclusion of a demand for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire consistent with resolution 2735 (2024), the release of all hostages and remains, unimpeded humanitarian access, the rejection of forced displacement and demographic change, accountability for violations, and support for the two-State solution. We also welcome the express mention of UNRWA and the need to support United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners, although we would have preferred a clearer reaffirmation of UNRWA’s central role and a dedicated call for its funding, as the humanitarian response cannot be sustained without it. Given the urgency of ending the suffering of civilians, securing the release of all hostages, and ensuring life-saving assistance reaches all those in need, Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We call on all parties to implement it fully and without delay.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan cannot support this unbalanced draft. While we strongly support the ceasefire, the release of all hostages and detainees, and unhindered humanitarian access, this text fails to condemn Israeli airstrikes and settler violence with the same clarity it applies to Hamas. It singles out Hamas while ignoring the occupation, the blockade, and the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination. Pakistan votes against this draft and calls for a balanced resolution that upholds international law and the two-State solution.
before.Panama: Panama will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because it addresses the Council’s most urgent and non-postponable responsibilities: demanding the immediate, full and expeditious implementation of the ceasefire agreement of 13 October 2025; insisting on the unconditional, dignified release of all remaining hostages and the return of the remains of the deceased; calling for immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access at scale to all civilians in Gaza; and rejecting forced displacement, starvation, collective punishment and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. We welcome that the text also reaffirms the two-State solution and the unification of Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority, while calling for accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law, including settler violence and attacks on holy sites. Panama supported the efforts of the elected members in previous negotiations, and we support this balanced text because it responds to the principles of the Charter and to the defence of human dignity. We urge all parties to comply fully with their obligations and to return without delay to a credible political process.
before.Republic of Korea: Thank you, Mr. President. The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the ceasefire agreement of 13 October and call for its immediate, full and expeditious implementation, including the release of all remaining hostages and the return of the remains of all deceased hostages, the release of Palestinian detainees, and the withdrawal of Israeli forces as provided for in the agreement. We remain gravely concerned by the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and by continuing violations of the ceasefire, including attacks against civilians and humanitarian personnel. We welcome the text’s call for immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access at scale through the United Nations humanitarian system, and for accountability for all violations, including settler violence and violence by Israeli forces in the West Bank. The Republic of Korea reiterates its unwavering support for the two-State solution and for Gaza to be unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. We urge all parties to respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians, and resume negotiations without delay.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation has consistently demanded an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to Gaza, including the lifting of the blockade. We engaged constructively on this draft and proposed amendments that would have condemned Israeli attacks against civilians on an equal basis, demanded the lifting of the humanitarian blockade under United Nations coordination, and supported a genuine international peace conference. Regrettably, the penholder rejected these essential corrections. The text remains unbalanced: it strongly condemns Hamas but does not explicitly name Israeli violations, including attacks on civilians and the blockade; it also seeks to prescribe external conditions for Palestinian governance. For these reasons, we cannot support this draft. At the same time, we do not wish to block the Council’s call for implementation of the ceasefire. The Russian Federation will therefore abstain.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the inclusion of our requested language on UNRWA’s safe and unhindered access throughout Gaza and on rejecting demographic or territorial change in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. At a time when the ceasefire remains fragile and the humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic, this Council must speak with one voice: for full implementation of the agreement, unhindered humanitarian access, the release of all hostages and remains, protection of civilians, accountability, and a credible path to the two-State solution. We call on all parties to comply with their obligations and on all Council members to support the implementation of this resolution.
before.Somalia: Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the incorporation of language protecting the mandate and operations of UNRWA and demanding the immediate cessation of settlement activities and settler violence. Given the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, the need to fully implement the ceasefire, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, protect civilians, release all hostages and detainees, and move credibly toward the two-State solution, the Council must act with urgency and unity. Somalia supports this resolution while stressing that its implementation must be immediate, complete and accountable.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. The ceasefire agreement of 13 October must be implemented immediately, fully and in good faith. All remaining hostages must be released, the remains of all deceased hostages returned, and Palestinian detainees released consistent with the agreement. We condemn Hamas in the strongest terms, including its attacks, hostage-taking and sexual violence, and we reiterate that Hamas must have no role in the future of Gaza. The humanitarian situation demands immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered access at scale, including through all crossings and for the United Nations humanitarian system. We welcome the explicit reference to UNRWA, which must be allowed to operate and be supported. Israel must respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and halt settlement expansion and settler violence, with accountability for all violations. The United Kingdom remains committed to the two-State solution and to a credible, irreversible and time-bound political process, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under a reformed Palestinian Authority. We call on all parties to implement this resolution without delay.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favour of this resolution, which we have submitted because the Security Council must speak clearly and with one voice on the situation in Gaza and the West Bank. This text welcomes the 13 October ceasefire agreement and demands its full and expeditious implementation, including the release of all remaining hostages and the return of all remains, the release of Palestinian detainees consistent with the agreement, the withdrawal of Israeli forces as provided for, and the safe return of Palestinian civilians. It condemns in the strongest terms Hamas’s horrific terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023, hostage-taking, conflict-related sexual violence, and the use of civilians and civilian infrastructure for military purposes. It also demands immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access at scale, rejects any forced displacement or demographic or territorial change, condemns settler violence and attacks on holy sites, and calls for accountability for all violations. The United States remains unwavering in its commitment to the two-State solution and to a reformed Palestinian Authority governing a unified Gaza and West Bank. We urge all Council members to support this balanced and necessary resolution.

after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan takes the floor to explain its vote against the resolution just adopted. Our vote was not against the ceasefire, nor against the release of hostages and detainees, nor against humanitarian relief for the people of Gaza. Pakistan has consistently supported those objectives. We voted against this text because it remains unbalanced and does not meet the basic requirements of international law and legitimacy.

The resolution condemns one party in the strongest terms while failing to clearly condemn Israeli military attacks against civilians, settler terrorism, the continued blockade, collective punishment, and the violation of the rights of the Palestinian people. It does not explicitly address the root causes of this crisis: occupation, settlement expansion, denial of self-determination, and the failure to implement the relevant United Nations resolutions. It also fails to uphold the principle that all violations of international humanitarian law must be condemned and addressed without selectivity.

Pakistan regrets that the Council has adopted a text that does not fully reflect the most fundamental rights of the Palestinian people, including their right to an independent and sovereign State of Palestine, with East Jerusalem as its capital, living side by side with Israel within the pre-1967 borders. We reject any attempt at demographic or territorial change in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and any forced displacement of the Palestinian people.

At the same time, Pakistan demands the immediate, full and complete implementation of the ceasefire agreement, the release of all remaining hostages and detainees, the withdrawal of Israeli forces in accordance with the agreement, and safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Gaza. The resolution's adoption must not become another exercise in selective implementation. The Security Council must remain seized of this matter and must act with the same urgency and seriousness to end the suffering of the Palestinian people.

Pakistan will continue to stand by the Palestinian people and their just cause in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and the enduring position of the people of Pakistan.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

Sierra Leone voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its adoption. We thank the United States for its efforts and all Council members for the constructive engagement that made this text possible. Its adoption must now be translated without delay into relief for civilians, dignity for hostages and their families, and a credible path away from the cycle of violence.

Sierra Leone remains gravely concerned by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and by continuing violations of the ceasefire. We unequivocally condemn the horrific terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October 2023, the taking and killing of hostages, conflict-related sexual violence, and the use of civilians and civilian infrastructure for military purposes. All remaining living hostages must be released immediately, unconditionally and with dignity, and the remains of all deceased hostages returned. We equally condemn all violations of international humanitarian law by any party, including attacks on civilians, attacks on humanitarian personnel, and the killing of civilians seeking humanitarian assistance, as well as settler violence and attacks on holy sites. Those responsible must be held accountable through prompt, independent and transparent investigations.

The 13 October ceasefire agreement must be implemented fully and expeditiously, including the withdrawal of Israeli forces as provided for and the safe return of Palestinian civilians to their homes and neighbourhoods throughout Gaza. Humanitarian access must be immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered at scale, through all crossings and through the United Nations humanitarian system, including UNRWA and all humanitarian partners. We reject forced displacement, starvation, collective punishment and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

Sierra Leone reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the two-State solution, consistent with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, and to the unity of the Gaza Strip with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. The Council has spoken. The measure of this resolution will be its implementation, and Sierra Leone will continue to support every effort to secure a just, lasting and comprehensive peace in the Middle East.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President, Somalia takes the floor to welcome the adoption of this resolution. We thank the penholder and all Council members whose efforts allowed the Council to speak with one voice at a moment of grave suffering. While the text is not perfect, its adoption sends a clear and urgent message: the ceasefire of 13 October must be implemented immediately, fully and in good faith; all remaining hostages must be released and the remains of the deceased returned; Palestinian detainees must be released consistent with the agreement; Israeli forces must withdraw as provided for; and safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access must reach all civilians throughout Gaza through the United Nations humanitarian system, including UNRWA.

Somalia stresses that implementation, not proclamation, is what will count. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians, refrain from all violations of the ceasefire, reject forced displacement and any demographic or territorial change in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and ensure accountability for violations. We also call for an immediate end to settler violence and settlement activity, and for a credible political horizon leading to the two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority.

The humanitarian catastrophe demands immediate action: crossings must open, aid must flow at scale, and food, water, medicine, shelter, fuel and essential services must reach those in need. We urge Member States to support UNRWA and humanitarian partners. Somalia will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and to support efforts to translate this resolution into protection, relief and a just and lasting peace.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States welcomes the adoption of this resolution, which we were proud to sponsor. With this vote, the Security Council has spoken with clarity on the ceasefire agreement of 13 October and on the urgent obligations that flow from it: full and expeditious implementation, the immediate and dignified release of all remaining hostages and return of all remains, release of Palestinian detainees consistent with the agreement, withdrawal of Israeli forces as provided for, and immediate, safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access at scale throughout Gaza.

The United States condemns in the strongest terms Hamas’s horrific terrorist attacks of 7 October 2023, its hostage-taking, conflict-related sexual violence, and its use of civilians and civilian infrastructure as shields. Hamas bears responsibility for the suffering of this war. It must have no role in the future of Gaza. We call on all parties to respect the ceasefire, protect civilians, facilitate humanitarian operations, and refrain from any action inconsistent with the agreement. We also call for accountability for all violations, including attacks on civilians, humanitarian personnel, and holy sites, and we reject any forced displacement or demographic and territorial change in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

The United States remains committed to Israel’s security and to the vision of a two-State solution, with Gaza unified with the West Bank under a reformed Palestinian Authority. We thank Egypt, Qatar, and all partners working to make this ceasefire durable. The test now is implementation. The United States will remain actively engaged to ensure that this resolution is translated into real relief for civilians, freedom for the hostages, and a credible political horizon. Thank you.
